name: @tokengate/gateway
description: Self-hosted credential broker for Cloudflare Workers: callers present a workload identity token (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC), the gateway injects the upstream API credential.

scripts.deploy: wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --remote && wrangler d1 migrations apply TELEMETRY_DB --remote && wrangler deploy
scripts.db:migrate:local: wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --local && wrangler d1 migrations apply TELEMETRY_DB --local
scripts.test:scripts: bash scripts/check-config.sh && bash test/security/check-config-test.sh && bash scripts/check-bundle.sh

DB.description: Control-plane database (users, caller providers, services, grants, settings, audit log). Created for you; `pnpm run deploy` applies its migrations.

TELEMETRY_DB.description: Request log and hourly rollups, kept separate so telemetry volume cannot fill the control plane. Created for you; `pnpm run deploy` applies its migrations.

TOKENGATE_KEK.description: **Required. Replace the default.** Key that encrypts stored upstream credentials: 32 random bytes, base64. The default from .dev.vars.example is public and the Worker refuses it outside local development. Generate your own outside Cloudflare with `openssl rand -base64 32` and keep a copy in your vault: losing it loses every stored credential. For rotation, see docs/operations/key-rotation.md in the repository.

AUTH_ACCESS_DEVELOPMENT.description: **Local development only.** Signs every admin request to localhost in as this email, with no check. In production it signs nobody in, and together with AUTH_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN and AUTH_ACCESS_AUD no login works: delete this secret and set the Access variables before you add services (stored credentials are bound to these variables).
